## Must-Fix 1 — two coupled test pins that the plan's own G7 edits deterministically break

The plan's §7(i) completeness grep is TOKEN-keyed
(`grep -rn 'cap-5\|cap5\|cap_5' tests/`) and therefore structurally cannot see
PROSE-literal anchors. Two exist, both pinning `steps/13-step-9.md` content that
G7 rewrites:

- `tests/test_issue_skill_neutral_gate_vocab_brief.py:93` —
  `s9a = text[start : text.index("Max 5 rounds per reviewer", start)]`. G7
  rewrites `steps/13-step-9.md:588` to "Max 10 rounds per reviewer", so
  `str.index` raises `ValueError` and `test_step9a_analyzer_respawn_by_reference`
  errors.
- `tests/test_issue_skill_humanize_verify_first_pin.py:63` —
  `_region(text, "**Procedural-only verdict strip", "**If REVISE (rounds 2-5):**")`,
  whose helper fail-louds on `end != -1` (line 51, live at line 103). G7 rewrites
  `steps/13-step-9.md:1632` to "(rounds 2-10)", so the end anchor vanishes and the
  `_strip_region` test fails.

Both are NEW suite failures vs the plan-time baseline, introduced by the plan's
own specified edits — so acceptance criterion 4 is unsatisfiable as written.

Fix: add both files to §4 and to the §10 atomicity set A (they pin steps/13
content), re-keying the two anchors to "Max 10 rounds per reviewer" and
"(rounds 2-10)"; and widen §7(i)'s tests-side verification from the bare token to
the full edited-literal family, e.g.

    grep -rniE 'max 5 rounds|rounds 2-5|round cap 5|up to 5 rounds|count\s*[<>]=?\s*5|revision_round\s*[<>]=?\s*5|cap \(5\)|at round 5|after round 5|5 rounds per reviewer' tests/

mapping every hit to either edit-in-same-commit or an enumerated out-of-scope
class.

Note on inheritance: #784's analogous "no test pins == 3" claim was TRUE at the
time. The pin population has grown since, so the claim must be RE-DERIVED per
raise, never inherited from the precedent.
